title: Christianity: the two commandments
hookLine: Jesus names the greatest commandments: love God, and love your neighbor as yourself (Matthew 22:37–40)
last: PESACH — WE WERE SLAVES, NOW FREE.

cards: Of all the commandments, which one is the greatest? There's no safe answer, and in the Gospel of Matthew a lawyer puts it to Jesus. The text says he asked it to test him.
Jewish tradition, written down later, counts six hundred and thirteen commandments in the Torah. Pick one, and you seem to shrug at the rest. Jesus doesn't pick one.
He picks two, and he picks them from the very scripture of last week's visit.

teach.h: LOVE GOD WITH ALL YOUR HEART.
teach.b: His answer, in the King James Version, Matthew twenty-two: "Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets."
If the first sounds familiar, it should. It comes from Deuteronomy, right beside the Shema from a week ago: hear, O Israel. The second comes from Leviticus, chapter nineteen.
Jesus, a Jewish teacher, is quoting the Torah, and many Christians treat his pairing as the center of their faith. Notice three things.
First, the order: God first, neighbor second, but the second is like unto it, the same kind of thing.
Many Christians say you can't really keep one without the other; a later New Testament letter says that someone who claims to love God and hates a brother is not telling the truth.

teach.h: ALL THE LAW HANGS ON THESE TWO.
teach.b: Second, the word hang: everything else hangs on these two, like a door on its hinges. Third, as thyself. It assumes you already know how you want to be treated, and asks you to aim that at someone else.
In Luke's Gospel, a lawyer asks the follow-up, and who is my neighbor?
Jesus answers with a story, the good Samaritan, in which the neighbor turns out to be the stranger no one expected.

how: Many Christians memorize the two great commandments, and some churches read them aloud in worship; churches of many traditions teach love of God and neighbor as the heart of the faith.

games.q: a lawyer asks Jesus to name the single greatest commandment. what does he answer?
o: one commandment, the first of the ten.
two: love God, and love your neighbor as yourself.
games.why: he pairs Deuteronomy and Leviticus, and says all the law and the prophets hang on them.

practice: Let faces come: the person next door, the coworker who seems tired, the stranger who serves your coffee. Pick one, and ask the as-yourself question: if I were them today, what small thing would I be glad of?
A hand with the bins, a real hello, a message; let the answer be small and doable.

wordCard.voice: Christianity, at its center: two commandments, love God and love your neighbor as yourself, on which all the law and the prophets hang. Today's word.
